lead.headline: KODAGU COURT SENTENCES MAN TO DEATH IN 2024 MURDER OF MINOR
lead.deck: A sessions court convicted Onkarappa in the killing of a 16-year-old girl. The sentence must be confirmed by the Karnataka High Court before it can be carried out.
paragraphs: A Kodagu sessions court sentenced Onkarappa to death for the 2024 murder of a 16-year-old girl, finding him guilty of murder and sexual assault. The judge also imposed a fine of ₹80,000 and ordered ₹16.5 lakh compensation for the victim’s family.
The case followed officials’ intervention to stop a proposed marriage while the girl was underage. The death sentence is subject to confirmation by the Karnataka High Court.

image.alt: The 16-year-old girl whose killing was heard by a Kodagu sessions court.
image.caption: A Kodagu sessions court sentenced Onkarappa; the death sentence requires High Court confirmation. Photo: Hindustan Times.

sidebarStory.headline: BWSSB PLANS 12-HOUR CAUVERY WATER SHUTDOWN TOMORROW
sidebarStory.subhead: Pumping will stop from 6am to 6pm Wednesday; residents are urged to store water.
paragraphs: The Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board says Cauvery pumping will be suspended across all stages on November 25 for urgent repair and maintenance at T.K. Halli, Harohalli and Tataguni.
The board asked residents to store enough water for daily needs. Its notice did not specify which localities may be affected.

image.caption: File photo: pipework at a water pumping station. Photo: The Bengaluru Live.

stories.headline: BENGALURU JATRE TO BRING 250 EVENTS FROM DECEMBER 4
paragraphs: A 10-day Bengaluru Jatre will run from December 4 to 13, with nearly 250 cultural events across the city. Its opening procession is set to feature about 500 folk artistes in 20 troupes along Brigade Road and M.G. Road.

stories.headline: MLA SUBMITS RESIGNATION LETTER OVER ELEPHANT RELOCATION
paragraphs: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation to the Assembly Speaker’s office in protest over an elephant relocation operation. The office received but has not accepted the letter; she warned the move could worsen human-elephant conflict.

stories.headline: BLUE LINE METRO TRIAL TRAIN TO ARRIVE AT DODDANEKKUNDI TODAY
paragraphs: A trial train for Bengaluru Metro’s Blue Line Phase 2A is scheduled to arrive at Doddanekkundi from K.R. Puram on November 24. This is a project milestone; passenger services are not beginning today.

groups.ariaLabel: India climate, public policy and parliamentary news

stories.headline: SUPREME COURT FAVOURS BS-VI-ONLY VEHICLES IN DELHI THROUGH WINTER
paragraphs: The Supreme Court said only vehicles meeting BS-VI emission standards should be allowed to ply in Delhi during winter as it considered measures to tackle seasonal air pollution. The observation concerns Delhi and is not a nationwide vehicle ban.

stories.headline: SUPREME COURT SEEKS RESPONSES ON ANTI-DEFECTION REFORM PLEA
paragraphs: The Supreme Court sought responses from the Centre, Election Commission and Law Commission on a plea for anti-defection reforms, including continuing disqualification proceedings after resignation and setting a decision deadline.

stories.headline: I4C ISSUES CYBER-HYGIENE ADVISORY ON WHATSAPP WEB
paragraphs: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre has urged public servants to avoid WhatsApp Web for official or sensitive work, following reports of suspicious access to defence-related groups.

stories.headline: 11 UNAUTHORISED IMPS TRANSFERS DRAIN ₹42.4 LAKH FROM BENGALURU FIRM
paragraphs: A Bengaluru company reported 11 unauthorised IMPS transfers totalling about ₹42.4 lakh within half an hour, despite two-level approval and OTP safeguards. Police are investigating the transactions.

stories.headline: GATHERINGS RESTRICTED IN MADURAI AROUND HILLTOP DEEPAM ROW
paragraphs: Madurai authorities restricted gatherings through November 25 after the Supreme Court allowed a one-time lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at a hilltop stone pillar on November 24. The order does not settle the wider dispute.

stories.headline: DELHI POLICE CONSTABLE SUSPENDED AFTER WEDDING CALLED OFF
paragraphs: A Delhi Police constable posted in Sonipat has been suspended after allegations that a wedding was called off over a car demand as dowry. The constable has denied demanding dowry, and the complaint is under inquiry.

groups.ariaLabel: Indian cricket, chess and hockey news

stories.headline: EAST BENGAL FACE MUST-WIN TEST AGAINST AL-HUSSEIN
paragraphs: East Bengal meet Jordan’s Al-Hussein in Kolkata on November 24 in an AFC Champions League Two group match. A defeat would end the Indian side’s campaign; kickoff is scheduled for 7:15pm IST.

stories.headline: SYED MODI INTERNATIONAL OPENS IN LUCKNOW
paragraphs: The Syed Modi India International, a BWF Super 300 tournament, begins in Lucknow on November 24 and runs through November 29.

stories.headline: INDIA AND NEW ZEALAND SHARE FIRST TEST AFTER DRAW
paragraphs: The opening Test ended in a draw after India declared at 720 for nine and New Zealand reached 239 for five in its second innings, 113 runs behind.
